skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with no hidden execution, but its broad automatic activation wording could cause it to run for unrelated requests.

dimensions.detail: The instructions prefer local-friendly scripts, templates, checklists, and CPU-safe workflows, and do not request unusual environment access, credential stores, broad indexing, or external API use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown guidance and a small YAML interface file only; no install scripts, executable files, package hooks, or command-running setup were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad trigger words such as security, every, must, pass, before, activate, and bug fix, and agents/openai.yaml enables implicit invocation, so it may be selected outside its intended SkillScan-style workflow context.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, session reuse, credential handling, or automatic data mutation is described in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to help users create SkillScan-style security workflows, checklists, analysis, and implementation support; that capability is coherent with the markdown instructions, but the framing also expands into broad work-productivity support.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a broadly triggered workflow-helper skill. It should be narrowed to explicit SkillScan-style security workflow requests before relying on implicit invocation, especially in workspaces where generic security or bug-fix requests should be routed elsewhere.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger and implicit-invocation concern is supported by the artifact text across SKILL.md, the README files, the Chinese skill file, agents/openai.yaml, and the requirement plan. I treat it as a real routing and reliability concern, but not as evidence of malicious behavior because the artifact is documentation-only and does not request hidden execution, sensitive data, persistence, or privileged access.
